subtopic: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions of Alkyl Halides
stem: The best method for preparation of alkyl fluorides is
Identify the chiral molecule from the following.

An alkyl chloride on Wurtz reaction gives 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. The same alkyl chloride on reduction with zinc-copper couple in alchol give hydrocarbon with molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). What is the structure of alkyl chloride
solution: [Textbook misprint: the fourth alternative is printed as \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CHCl}\), whose last carbon is written \(\mathrm{CHCl}\) and so has only three bonds. It is transcribed exactly as printed. Read as the intended \(\mathrm{CH_2Cl}\) it would be 1-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane, which is a six-carbon halide and still fails the question's own test, since reduction would give 2,3-dimethylbutane \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) and not \(\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}\). The answer is unaffected either way.]

stem: Choose the compound from the following that will react fastest by \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism.

\(\mathrm{C_6H_{11}-Cl} + \mathrm{Mg} \xrightarrow[\text{ether}]{\text{dry}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{B}\)

(the ring drawn in the book is a plain saturated six-membered ring, i.e. \(\mathrm{C_6H_{11}-}\) is cyclohexyl)

The product 'B' in the above reaction sequence is,

options.label: C
options.text: \(\mathrm{Cl-C_6H_{10}-Mg}\) (Cl and Mg on opposite carbons of one cyclohexane ring)
